Thought: I need to determine what gases can be generated when alcohols/polyols react with alkali metals and strong reducing agents.

When alcohols (R-OH) react with alkali metals like sodium (Na), potassium (K), or lithium (Li), they undergo a reaction where the metal replaces the hydrogen in the hydroxyl group, producing hydrogen gas:

R-OH + Na → R-ONa + H₂

Similarly, when polyols (compounds with multiple hydroxyl groups) react with alkali metals, they also produce hydrogen gas.

With strong reducing agents (like sodium hydride, lithium aluminum hydride), alcohols can also produce hydrogen gas as these reagents donate hydride ions that can combine with the proton from the alcohol.

Looking at the options:
A. Carbon dioxide - Not typically produced in these reactions
B. Hydrogen gas - This is produced when alcohols react with alkali metals
C. Nitrogen gas - Not produced in these reactions
D. Oxygen gas - Not produced in these reactions

The correct answer is B. Hydrogen gas.
